extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners authorized to practice before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO reciprocal-discipline proceedings; OED staff and USPTO counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing USPTO imposition of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner is disciplined by a state authority, including notice requirements, possible defenses, disciplinary outcomes, and administrative steps (publication, notifications, dissociation from customer numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted state authority; here, discipline is predicated upon Respondent's 90-day suspension by the State of Michigan Attorney Discipline Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline proceedings are initiated by the OED Director filing a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and issuing a Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must be sent to the respondent (here by certified mail) and provide the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verifiable delivery (e.g., certified mail with receipt number), state the 40-day deadline, and inform respondent of the procedural basis and possible defenses under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Available defenses to reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline based on one or more specified reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must advise the respondent of these defenses; failure to assert them timely may result in waiver. (The order notes Respondent did not file a response.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicative standard when respondent fails to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not timely respond to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond supports entry of the identical discipline absent contested factual issues; the USPTO treats non-response as lack of opposition to the imposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary sanction imposed (duration and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for ninety (90) days, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders should specify duration, scope (e.g., trademark and non-patent practice), and effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of statutory/regulatory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary actions are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (and violations such as 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) may be cited as the basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders should cite the controlling statutes/regulations that authorize reciprocal discipline and identify the specific rules violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette (content and consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with specified text describing the Respondent, the suspension, the rule violated, the predicate state action, and availability of disciplinary decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the materially-consistent notice language (sample provided in the order), identify the respondent's city/state, the scope of practice affected, citation of the violation, summary of the state proceeding and findings, and a reference/URL to OED's FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 11.59 procedures to notify relevant state agencies, courts, and public channels of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's duties upon discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent is required to comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following imposition of public discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders should reference § 11.58 and require compliance (the order here does not recite § 11.58 duties verbatim but mandates compliance). Practitioners must consult § 11.58 for specific post-discipline obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps must be taken to remove the disciplined practitioner's access/association with USPTO electronic customer accounts and certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders should expressly bar seeking or being added to customer credentials for the duration of suspension and until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary records
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders should provide or reference the public repository where the decision and related disciplinary records can be accessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds cited from the predicate state proceeding (examples of misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: The predicate state order described admissions and findings: conviction for allowing an unlicensed person to operate a motor vehicle, inaccuracies in responding to an investigation request, failure to disclose facts to correct a misapprehension, and violations of specified Michigan Court Rules and MRPC provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reciprocal discipline is predicated on state findings, the USPTO order may summarize the underlying misconduct (convictions, ethics violations) that formed the state discipline basis.
